papers.title: Surrogate-Based probabilistic assessment of hydrogen leakage through abandoned wells in depleted gas reservoirs for underground hydrogen storage
A Physics‐Based, Lumped‐Parameter Model for Attributing Natural and Anthropogenic CO2 Emissions From Producing Geothermal Systems
papers.summary: We built a lumped-parameter physics model of CO2 in a producing geothermal reservoir and calibrated it to two New Zealand fields. At Rotokawa, we estimate that metering the power plant overcounts the human-caused change in emissions by 17–45 kt a year, because production reduces natural CO2 discharge at the surface.

papers.title: Socio-economic value of data-driven eruption forecasts to balance false alarms against catastrophic loss
papers.summary: We compared the cost of false alarms with the loss from missed eruptions for eruption forecasts at five volcanoes. In retrospective tests, with documented losses at two volcanoes and assumed losses at three, acting on the forecasts could have reduced losses by 30 to 90%, despite many false alarms.

papers.title: A Machine‐Learning Classification for Torlesse Composite Terrane Petrofacies and its Application to Sediment Provenance
papers.journal: New Zealand Journal of Geology and Geophysics

papers.title: From forecast skill to economic value: sub-hourly wildfire potential forecasting across Australian regions
Impacts of reservoir permeability anisotropy on hydrogen migration and recovery efficiency in geological storage
Effects of reservoir interlayers on hydrogen migration and distribution in underground hydrogen storage
Determination of interfacial tension for H2-H2S-water and CH4-H2S-water mixtures under different geological conditions for underground hydrogen storage
Preferential seawater intrusion in a heterogeneous alluvial aquifer that extends offshore: Insights from numerical modeling
Advanced Hydrogeochemical Coupling in Carbon Sequestration: A 4D Spatiotemporal Fourier Neural Operator–Driven Modeling Framework
The Research and Impact of the Works by Don Nield
Quantifying Interannual Variations in Groundwater Fluxes Within a Braidplain Aquifer Using Active‐Distributed Temperature Sensing
Impact of operational parameters on water invasion in underground hydrogen storage: A numerical investigation of the Ahuroa field, New Zealand
Forecasting Eruptions at Steamboat Geyser: Time Scales, Differentiability, and Detectability of Seismic Precursors Through Data‐Driven Methods
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Machine Learning and Computation
papers.summary: A machine learning model trained on signals in the 2018 seismic record of Steamboat Geyser showed a fair ability to separate pre-eruption periods from other times in later data. Its eruption probability peaked at 12.6% within 18 hours of an eruption, compared with 8.1% from eruption intervals alone.

papers.title: Ergodic seismic precursors and transfer learning for short term eruption forecasting at data scarce volcanoes
papers.summary: We trained forecasting models on seismic data from 41 eruptions at 24 volcanoes and tested each on a volcano left out of training. They scored better than a seismic amplitude benchmark and, at three volcanoes, close to models trained on that volcano alone. This suggests precursors are shared between volcanoes.

papers.title: Sub-hourly forecasting of fire potential using machine learning on time series of surface weather variables
Techno-economic analysis of geothermal combined with direct and biomass-based carbon dioxide removal for high-temperature hydrothermal systems
Influence of hydrogen sulfide on gas-water interface in underground hydrogen storage: A molecular dynamics study
Earthquakes Trigger Rapid Flash Boiling Front at Optimal Geologic Conditions
papers.summary: An earthquake can make hot water boil in the fracture between two faults. In our models this flashing was limited, and complete flashing is highly unlikely. Opening was largest where the faults were separated by about 10% of their length and overlapped by about 2.5%.

papers.title: From carbon neutral to carbon negative: a theoretical bioenergy and CO2 removal retrofit at Ngāwhā geothermal power station
papers.journal: Journal of the Royal Society of New Zealand

papers.title: Multitimescale Template Matching: Discovering Eruption Precursors across Diverse Volcanic Settings
Prospectivity analysis for underground hydrogen storage, Taranaki basin, Aotearoa New Zealand: A multi-criteria decision-making approach
Eruption Forecasting Model for Copahue Volcano (Southern Andes) Using Seismic Data and Machine Learning: A Joint Interpretation with Geodetic Data (GNSS and InSAR)
Testing the reproducibility of active-distributed temperature sensing for measuring groundwater specific discharge beneath a braided river
Molecular dynamics insights into gas-water interfacial tension: Optimizing hydrogen storage in subsurface conditions
Active-distributed temperature sensing dataset beneath a braided river
Shallow groundwater characterisation and hydrograph classification in the coastal city of Ōtautahi/Christchurch, New Zealand
Using Template Matching to Detect Hidden Fluid Release Episodes Beneath Crater Lakes in Ruapehu, Copahue, and Kawah Ijen Volcanoes
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
papers.summary: We searched Ruapehu seismic data from 2006 to 2021 for a tremor pattern seen before the 2019 Whakaari eruption. We then looked for a tremor peak and exponential decay after each match. Six events passed, including a 2009 event that we classify as a fluid release into the crater lake.

papers.title: Association Between Injection and Microseismicity in Geothermal Fields With Multiple Wells: Data‐Driven Modeling of Rotokawa, New Zealand, and Húsmúli, Iceland
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
papers.summary: We used data-driven methods to find which injection wells are associated with small earthquakes at the Rotokawa (New Zealand) and Húsmúli (Iceland) fields. Injection was more closely associated with earthquake rates averaged over weeks than over days. At Rotokawa, we found no evidence that rapid injection changes trigger earthquakes.

papers.title: Identification of Seismo‐Volcanic Regimes at Whakaari/White Island (New Zealand) Via Systematic Tuning of an Unsupervised Classifier
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
papers.summary: We tuned an unsupervised classifier on 12.5 years of volcanic tremor at Whakaari. It separated background from unrest. In a retrospective analysis, its output changed to unrest regimes 6 weeks before the August 2012 eruption and about 3.5 months before the December 2019 eruption.

papers.title: Physics-Based Forecasting of Induced Seismicity at Groningen Gas Field, The Netherlands: Post Hoc Evaluation and Forecast Update
papers.summary: We tested our 2017 earthquake forecast for the Groningen gas field against the earthquakes that followed, then updated it. For 2021 to 2030, the largest event has a 1% chance of exceeding magnitude 3.8 if ruptures are confined to the reservoir, and 5.4 if they can extend below it.

papers.title: Carbon negative geothermal: Theoretical efficiency and sequestration potential of geothermal-BECCS energy cycles
papers.journal: International Journal of Greenhouse Gas Control

papers.title: Active distributed temperature sensing to assess surface water–groundwater interaction and river loss in braided river systems
Evaluation of short-term probabilistic eruption forecasting at Whakaari, New Zealand
papers.summary: We ran an eruption forecaster at Whakaari for 18 months and filtered out the earthquakes that caused its three false positives. In a test with the 2019 eruption withheld from training, a calibrated version gave a 2 to 4% chance in 48 hours, up to 400 times its lowest level.

papers.title: Seismic precursors to the Whakaari 2019 phreatic eruption are transferable to other eruptions and volcanoes
papers.summary: We searched seismic tremor recorded before 18 eruptions at six volcanoes for a shared precursor. A rise in the ratio of medium- to high-frequency tremor recurred before steam-driven eruptions at Whakaari and, less clearly, Ruapehu and Tongariro. At Whakaari in 2019, we interpret it as shallow sealing and pressurisation.

papers.title: Techno-Economic feasibility of enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) with partially bridging Multi-Stage fractures for district heating applications
Hydrothermal Cooling as a Requirement for Short Storage of Silicic Magmas
papers.summary: Magma for large eruptions in New Zealand's Taupō Volcanic Zone appears to have crystallised within decades to centuries. In our calculations, conduction through rock took over 1,000 years to remove the heat. Circulating groundwater above the magma, with a heat output of about 1,000 MW, could remove it within decades.

papers.title: A three-dimensional coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical numerical model with partially bridging multi-stage contact fractures in horizontal-well enhanced geothermal system
papers.journal: International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences
papers.summary: We propose a geothermal well design in which fractures grow alternately from the injection and production wells and stop short of the other well. In our model, this forces water through the rock between fractures and keeps produced water hotter, for the same mass produced, than fractures joining both wells.

papers.title: Heat Transfer Through the Wairakei‐Tauhara Geothermal System Quantified by Multi‐Channel Data Modeling
papers.summary: We combined electrical surveys, clay tests on drill cuttings, and well temperature logs to map the clay layer above the Wairakei-Tauhara geothermal reservoir. We estimate that 380 ± 21 MW of heat passes up through this layer. We treat this as a lower bound on the field's total heat output.

papers.title: Bayesian magnetotelluric inversion using methylene blue structural priors for imaging shallow conductors in geothermal fields
papers.summary: We developed a way to map the clay layer above a geothermal reservoir from electrical surveys, using clay tests on drill cuttings to reduce the range of possible depths. At Wairākei it returned depth ranges for the layer's boundaries and reduced the uncertainty in the depth of its base.

papers.title: Two-dimensional numerical modelling of strategies to avoid thermal stress induced flow channeling in fractured geothermal reservoirs
Ground motion simulation of hypothetical earthquakes in the upper North Island of New Zealand
papers.journal: New Zealand Journal of Geology and Geophysics
papers.summary: We simulated the largest credible earthquakes on two faults near Auckland, Hamilton and Tauranga. Sediment basins beneath the Hauraki Rift and Hamilton amplified slow shaking two to three times. A Wairoa North Fault earthquake gave 0.45 g, almost half of gravity, at Auckland's Mangatawhiri Dam.

papers.title: Automatic precursor recognition and real-time forecasting of sudden explosive volcanic eruptions at Whakaari, New Zealand
papers.summary: We trained a machine learning model on nine years of seismic tremor from one station at Whakaari. It recognised four-hour tremor bursts before most eruptions. In tests on eruptions withheld from its training, it warned of four of five eruptive episodes, including 17 hours before the fatal 2019 eruption.

papers.title: Response of Induced Seismicity to Injection Rate Reduction: Models of Delay, Decay, Quiescence, Recovery, and Oklahoma
papers.summary: We modelled how injection-triggered earthquakes respond to a cut in injection rate. The earthquake rate can fall by more than the cut and stop for a time before it partly recovers. For Western Oklahoma, our forecasts suggest the 2016 volume limit is inadequate.

papers.title: Microseismicity Cloud Can Be Substantially Larger Than the Associated Stimulated Fracture Volume: The Case of the Paralana Enhanced Geothermal System
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
papers.summary: During the 2011 Paralana geothermal stimulation in South Australia, earthquakes occurred up to 400 m from the well. Our inversion of the earthquake and well data suggests that permeability increased only within 40 m of it. For the best-fitting model, the stimulated volume was 0.4% of the seismically active volume.

papers.title: Physics‐based forecasting of induced seismicity at Groningen gas field, the Netherlands
papers.summary: We developed a physics-based model of the earthquakes caused by gas extraction at Groningen, calibrated it on about 600 recorded events, and forecast earthquakes from 2017 to 2024. Under each of three extraction rates, the largest event had a 5% chance of exceeding magnitude 4.0.

papers.title: Simulation of the crystal growth of platelet sea ice with diffusive heat and mass transfer
Collective properties of injection‐induced earthquake sequences: 2. Spatiotemporal evolution and magnitude frequency distributions
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
papers.summary: In our model, earthquakes triggered by rising fluid pressure include a higher proportion of small events than tectonic earthquakes. Pressure lowers the static strength of a fault faster than its residual strength. Modelling the 2010–2011 Guy-Greenbrier sequence in Arkansas, we estimated a fault permeability of 5 × 10⁻¹² m².

papers.title: Collective properties of injection‐induced earthquake sequences: 1. Model description and directivity bias
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
papers.summary: We modelled large catalogues of earthquakes triggered by injecting fluid into a fault. In our model, these ruptures tended to propagate back towards the injection well, where high fluid pressure favours continued rupture. In the strongest case, a sample of three modelled ruptures was enough to detect this bias.

papers.title: Hydraulic fracturing fluid migration in the subsurface: A review and expanded modeling results
papers.summary: We modelled fracturing fluid injected into shale 1,500 m below a drinking water aquifer. In our model, no fluid reached the aquifer without a permeable pathway such as a fault or leaky well. Where a pathway existed, modelling well production and imbibition reduced the amount reaching the aquifer tenfold.

papers.title: Numerical modeling of injection, stress and permeability enhancement during shear stimulation at the Desert Peak Enhanced Geothermal System
papers.journal: International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences
papers.summary: In 2010, cold water injected below the pressure that opens fractures raised the injectivity of well 27-15 at Desert Peak by an order of magnitude. Our model suggests cooling, and the stresses it caused, kept fractures failing where overpressure was too low. Pressure was still needed to push water in.

papers.title: Reducing uncertainty associated with CO2 injection and brine production in heterogeneous formations
papers.journal: International Journal of Greenhouse Gas Control
papers.summary: When CO2 is injected while brine is pumped out nearby, unknown variations in rock permeability make the outcome hard to predict. In a synthetic reservoir, permeability measured at five wells narrowed 30-year prediction ranges by 40 to 72%. Pressure tests between wells narrowed two of these ranges further.

papers.title: Passive injection: A strategy for mitigating reservoir pressurization, induced seismicity and brine migration in geologic CO2 storage
papers.journal: International Journal of Greenhouse Gas Control
papers.summary: We propose passive injection, in which pumping brine out of a reservoir draws CO2 in without raising reservoir pressure. In our models, a closed reservoir 3 km deep stored up to about 4 million tonnes of CO2 a year, with about 1.7 tonnes of brine produced per tonne stored.

papers.title: Insights into interconnections between the shallow and deep systems from a natural CO2 reservoir near Springerville, Arizona
papers.journal: International Journal of Greenhouse Gas Control

papers.title: Modeling caprock bending stresses and their potential for induced seismicity during CO2 injection
papers.journal: International Journal of Greenhouse Gas Control
papers.summary: In our models, CO2 injection at overpressures of 5 to 10 MPa bent the caprock and induced stresses of about 1 to 2 MPa in it, outside the zone of raised fluid pressure. Such stresses would be enough to reactivate an undetected, well-oriented, critically stressed fault near the well.

papers.title: Hydrological effects of dip‐slip fault rupture on a hydrothermal plume
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
papers.summary: We modelled a hot-water plume beside a normal fault in New Zealand's Taupō Volcanic Zone. A modelled magnitude 5.7 earthquake tripled water outflow, but within 20 days the excess fell below 10% of natural outflow. Fault damage caused a lasting rise in flow and moved upflow away from the fault.

papers.title: Delineation of catchment zones of geothermal systems in large‐scale rifted settings
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
papers.summary: We modelled circulation in a rift like New Zealand's Taupō Volcanic Zone and traced water from ten modelled geothermal fields to where it entered the ground. Their catchments cover 70 to 500 km² and increase with field heat output. Most water spends 5,000 to 50,000 years underground.

papers.title: Geometric properties of platelet ice crystals
papers.summary: We cut ten closely spaced slices from Antarctic sea ice and rebuilt its crystals in 3-D. For large, elongated grains, the outline in a photograph gave the horizontal direction of the c-axis with a standard deviation of 6°. Grain shape can also depend on the angle of the cut.

papers.title: The role of frictional plasticity in the evolution of normal fault systems
papers.summary: We modelled a single normal fault in a stretching crust. In our model the fault takes up about half of the stretching of the upper crust. Slow frictional shearing takes up the rest, mostly in the hanging wall, where we suggest new faults are favoured to form.

papers.title: Modeling the effects of silica deposition and fault rupture on natural geothermal systems
papers.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
papers.summary: We modelled a geothermal field in New Zealand's Taupō Volcanic Zone where cooling water deposits silica. Over 120,000 years, a low-permeability layer about 200 m thick formed at the surface. It diverted water sideways and warmed the reservoir. A fault rupturing the layer took at least 10,000 years to reseal.

papers.title: Energetics of normal earthquakes on dip-slip faults
papers.summary: We modelled a normal fault in a stretching crust and quantified where energy is released and taken up during each earthquake. Stored elastic energy lifts the footwall. The hangingwall drops under gravity and compresses the crust. We suggest the energy for normal faulting comes from gravity and stored elastic energy.

papers.title: Evolution of supercooling under coastal Antarctic sea ice during winter
Observation and modeling of platelet ice fabric in McMurdo Sound, Antarctica
papers.summary: Ice crystals that grow in supercooled water from beneath Antarctic ice shelves are frozen into sea ice. Using ice cores and a crystal growth model, we infer that western McMurdo Sound received a larger and more persistent supply of these crystals than the east in 2007.
